Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eurostat/searoute/88a2e568a8e0144d1f5a81c3931a7bc2bcce6901/modules/core/src/main/resources/marnet/marnet_plus_5km.gpkg
Modified for Shark on 2026-10-23: coordinates quantized to 1e-6 degrees and converted into indexed edges, with original passage attributes retained. Human-readable transformed data: network-source.json in this directory.
The network follows common shipping routes and includes European AIS-derived lines, based on the Oak Ridge National Labs CTA Transportation Network Group Global Shipping Lane Network (2000), as described by the upstream project.
Shark uses an independently implemented TypeScript shortest-path router; no upstream Java code was copied. Dover uses separate directional corridors. Polar passages and Corinth Canal are disabled by default (vessel/ice restrictions are not modeled by the current UI). Some port/river approaches remain approximate.
Additional Paraná river centerline: Natural Earth ne_10m_rivers_lake_centerlines, public domain, https://www.naturalearthdata.com/about/terms-of-use/
Planning and visualization only; not a navigation chart or a guarantee of navigability.
